title: Intel Confirms Long-Standing Microprocessor Chip Hacking Vulnerability
summary: Intel confirmed a security vulnerability in its microprocessor chips, affecting devices dating back to 1995, which could allow hackers to obtain personal information. The flaw, also found in chips by Arm and AMD, exploits predictive processing algorithms. While Intel asserts the exploits cannot corrupt or delete data, the initial patch is expected to slow operating times, and the company is working with others to provide updates.

title: Hacking fears: Security flaws put virtually all phones, computers at risk
summary: Security researchers have disclosed major flaws, Meltdown and Spectre, affecting chips from Intel, AMD, and ARM, which could allow hackers to steal sensitive information from nearly all modern computing devices. While Meltdown, specific to Intel, is more severe in the short term but patchable, Spectre affects a broader range of devices and is harder to fix, posing a long-term challenge. Companies like Intel, ARM, Google, Apple, and Microsoft are working on and releasing patches, though some suggest potential performance impacts on Intel chips.

title: Intel admits vulnerability, but plays down effects; stock slides, AMD gains
summary: Intel Corp. acknowledged a vulnerability in its chips requiring software patches, while disputing reports that the flaw is unique to its products and would significantly impact performance. The company's stock experienced its worst day in eight months, though it pared earlier losses. Rival Advanced Micro Devices Inc. (AMD) stated there was a "near zero" chance its chips would be affected.

title: Microsoft invests in Adaptive Biotechnologies to develop blood test to detect diseases
summary: Microsoft is partnering with Seattle-based Adaptive Biotechnologies to develop a universal blood test capable of detecting diseases in their early stages by mapping and understanding immune-system responses. Microsoft has made a significant, multi-million dollar investment in Adaptive as part of its Healthcare NExT initiative, leveraging its AI and machine learning capabilities for the project. While a universal test is about a decade away, intermediate tests are expected sooner, aiming to use the immune system's insights for early diagnosis.

title: Intel Shares Fall as Investors Worry About Costs of Chip Flaw
summary: Intel's shares fell due to investor concerns about the financial and reputational fallout from recently disclosed security flaws in its microprocessors. The flaws could allow hackers to steal sensitive information, leading to potential lawsuits and demands for compensation from major customers. The incident is also expected to increase Intel's chip development spending on security and could lead cloud companies to seek lower chip prices.
source: VOA - Voice of America English News
source_domain: VOA - Voice of America English News

title: U.S. fund managers expect value stocks to jump in 2018
summary: U.S. fund managers are shifting their focus to value stocks in early 2018, anticipating a jump in overlooked shares after a strong year for growth stocks in 2017. Despite past trends where growth stocks continued to lead after strong market years, some managers are actively underweighting technology and increasing positions in financials, industrial companies, and retailers with attractive valuations. They see these value-oriented investments as having significant upside potential over the next couple of years.

title: CAE Healthcare releases CAE LucinaAR, first childbirth simulator with augmented reality for clinical team training
summary: CAE Healthcare has launched CAE LucinaAR, the world's first childbirth simulator with augmented reality and integrated mother-baby physiology, using Microsoft HoloLens. This innovation allows clinical teams to practice emergency labor and delivery maneuvers with 3D holograms guiding the process. The initial module focuses on managing shoulder dystocia, aiming to improve mother-baby safety and provide immersive training experiences for healthcare professionals.

title: Gartner estimates Apple Mac grew shipments 1.4% in holiday quarter; computer market declined in Q417 and for the year
summary: Gartner reported that worldwide PC shipments declined by 2% in Q4 2017 and 2.8% for the full year, marking the 13th consecutive quarter of decline. Despite this, Apple's Mac shipments saw a modest 1.4% growth in the holiday quarter. The report highlighted a shift in the PC market towards specialized, high-quality devices and a significant decline in the U.S. market due to competition from other holiday gift items.

title: Equinix to Build More Owned Data Centers with “Nodes” for Cloud Giants
summary: Equinix plans to build more owned data centers with 1MW to 2MW "nodes" specifically for hyper-scale cloud and SaaS providers, including Amazon Web Services, Microsoft Azure, Google Cloud Platform, Facebook, and Apple. This strategy aims to capture the next wave of cloud deployments and secure competitive advantage by attracting profitable enterprise customers, despite lower margins compared to retail cabinet deployments. The company also continues its M&A strategy, including recent acquisitions of Verizon data centers and Metronode in Australia, expanding its global footprint.

title: Palo Alto Networks opens new office in Tel Aviv
summary: Palo Alto Networks has opened a new office and R&D center in Tel Aviv due to significant growth in its local research team. This Tel Aviv site is the only R&D center for Palo Alto Networks outside of its global headquarters in Santa Clara and is expected to see continued growth in employees. The company's expansion in Israel follows its acquisitions of Cyvera in 2014 and LightCyber in 2017.

title: Could this company become Chicago's own Salesforce?
summary: Relativity, a Chicago-based legal software company, has grown into a significant player in the e-discovery market, used by almost all of the nation's largest law firms. Led by CEO Andrew Sieja, the company is often compared to Salesforce for its platform approach and is considered a "unicorn" with potential IPO prospects. Despite being a dominant player, Relativity faces challenges from cloud-native rivals and has recently launched its own cloud product to stay competitive.

title: Apple, Oracle and Microsoft are expected to issue less debt in 2018
summary: Following five years of significant growth in corporate bond issuance, technology companies like Apple Inc., Broadcom Ltd., and Microsoft Corp. are projected to issue less debt in 2018. This shift is primarily due to the expectation that these companies will begin repatriating cash held overseas back to the U.S. after the new tax bill, alleviating the need to issue bonds for shareholder rewards.

title: What’s Changed: Gartner 2017 Magic Quadrant for Identity Governance and Administration (IGA)
summary: This article reviews the Gartner 2017 Magic Quadrant for Identity Governance and Administration (IGA), analyzing key changes since 2016 and significant trends in the market. It highlights shifts in vendor positioning, the growing "race to the cloud," increased adoption of analytics for risk analysis, and the emerging integration of User and Entity Behavior Analytics (UEBA). The report evaluates 13 vendors based on their ability to execute and completeness of vision in the IGA market.

title: The YouTube and Instagram secret that Google and Facebook don’t want you to know
summary: The article discusses how Alphabet (Google) and Facebook do not disclose the financial performance of YouTube and Instagram, respectively, despite these being immensely popular apps. This lack of transparency contrasts with Microsoft, which reports LinkedIn's revenue. The author suggests that the financial success of YouTube and Instagram is a significant driver for their parent companies, yet their exact contributions remain hidden from investors.

title: Columbia Sportswear activates Microsoft Cloud to strengthen consumer engagement
summary: Columbia Sportswear Co. is collaborating with Microsoft to enhance its global consumer experience and drive digital transformation through Microsoft Dynamics 365 and Azure. This initiative aims to provide a more personalized, seamless consumer experience by leveraging intelligent cloud technology for retail, call center, CRM, and merchandising operations, enabling better insights and efficiency.

title: Into the woods: Columbia Sportswear adopts Microsoft cloud
summary: Columbia Sportswear has adopted Microsoft's cloud services, including Dynamics 365 and Azure, to enhance customer experience, personalize interactions, and improve omnichannel capabilities. The move aims to drive insights from various consumer touchpoints and addresses the retail industry's increasing dependence on customer data analysis. This strategy allows Columbia to better understand customer desires and manage data at a rapid pace in an evolving retail landscape.

title: Heidrick & Struggles Appoints Avanade CEO Adam Warby to Board of Directors
summary: Heidrick & Struggles has appointed Adam Warby, CEO of Avanade, to its Board of Directors. Warby brings over 30 years of strategic leadership and consulting experience, with a focus on digital transformation and emerging technologies. His appointment is expected to enhance the firm's focus on skills and insights needed in the digital world.

title: Alphabet Inc Releases Q4 2017 Results; Traffic Acquisition Costs Increase 33%, Net Income Shows Loss Due To One-Time $10 Billion Tax Charge
summary: Alphabet Inc. reported its Q4 2017 results, revealing a 33% increase in Traffic Acquisition Costs (TAC) and a net loss due to a one-time $10 billion tax charge from the U.S. Tax Cuts and Jobs Act. Despite the tax impact, the company saw strong revenue growth, especially in its Cloud business which reached $1 billion in quarterly sales, and significant advancements in its 'Made by Google' hardware division, particularly with the Pixel 2. Alphabet also outlined plans for future growth in digital advertising, hardware, and AI, including an $8.6 billion share buyback and investment of repatriated earnings.

title: Former Intel executive Renee James launches Ampere, a new Arm-based server chip company
summary: Former Intel president Renee James has launched Ampere Computing, a new company focused on Arm-based server processors. Ampere has developed "Skylark," a 32-core Arm-based server processor, and aims to challenge Intel's dominance in the data center market at a time when Intel is facing security concerns. The company is backed by The Carlyle Group and plans to ship its chips later this year.

title: Coupa Software Teams Up with Tuition.io
summary: Coupa Software has partnered with Tuition.io to offer its U.S. full-time employees a student loan debt reduction program, including monthly disbursements to help pay down loan principal. This initiative extends to parents who took out Parent PLUS loans and reinforces Coupa's commitment to a people-centered corporate culture amidst the rising student debt crisis. Tuition.io recently secured $7 million in funding, bringing its total capital to over $115 million, and continues to expand its partnerships with major organizations.

title: The Trade Desk Reaps Rewards Of Growing Programmatic Advertising Market It Helped Create
summary: The Trade Desk, a programmatic demand-side platform, is benefiting significantly from the burgeoning programmatic advertising market it helped establish. The company's founder and CEO, Jeff Green, who envisioned the market's trajectory beginning in the early 2000s, discusses their strategy to compete with large entities like Google and Facebook by remaining objective and empowering ad agencies. Green also highlights the future potential in programmatic TV advertising, aiming to enhance transparency and effectiveness in the media ecosystem.

title: HP Inc. Rounds Out Its Printer Voice Command Capabilities With Amazon Alexa
summary: HP Inc. has expanded its printer voice command capabilities to include Amazon Alexa, adding to its existing support for Google Home and Microsoft Cortana. This move follows HP's initial integration of voice commands into its printers last year and positions the company as a leader in bringing classic home components into the smart home ecosystem. The article suggests future enhancements could include printer troubleshooting via voice and integrated smart assistants directly in printers.

title: Quorum OnQ 4.0
summary: Quorum OnQ 4.0, a backup and disaster recovery appliance, has added one-click recovery and new deduplication capabilities. Developed initially for U.S. naval combat systems, the updated version offers automated data recovery through virtual clones of production servers and is available in hardware, software, and as a cloud service. Judges lauded Quorum OnQ 4.0 as an "excellent solution" with strong automation and instant recovery features for the midmarket.

title: Never mind doubling down, Oracle is quadrupling cloud-based data centers
summary: Oracle announced plans to build 12 new cloud-based data centers, quadrupling its current total, to compete directly with cloud leaders like Amazon, Google, and Microsoft. This expansion is one of Oracle's largest infrastructure projects, aiming to boost its minimal market share in the cloud data-center space despite high capital expenses and existing market dominance by competitors.

title: Wipro, Tata Steel among 135 most ethical companies
summary: Wipro Limited and Tata Steel Ltd have been recognized among the 135 "world's most ethical companies" for 2018 by the US-based Ethisphere Institute. This marks the fifth consecutive year for some companies to be listed, highlighting that ethical business practices are rewarded with trust from employees, customers, and investors, and result in superior financial performance. The selected companies from 23 countries across 57 industries outperformed the large cap sector by significant margins over five and three years.

title: Microsoft hires Lindsay Rae McIntyre, former HR sued by IBM
summary: Microsoft has hired Lindsay Rae McIntyre, former IBM executive, as its new chief diversity officer, a move that has led to IBM suing McIntyre for violating a one-year non-compete agreement. IBM claims McIntyre possessed sensitive information about its diversity strategies and is seeking to enforce the non-competition agreement and recover equity compensation. McIntyre's lawyers state that Microsoft has no interest in IBM's trade secrets and McIntyre will not use old information in her new role.

title: Teleoperated Robots: The Industrial Future Using AR and VR
summary: Teleoperated robots, currently used in medical surgeries and military operations, are evolving with Virtual Reality (VR) and Augmented Reality (AR) technologies. MIT's CSAIL has developed a VR-based controller using an Oculus Rift headset, allowing human operators to control robots remotely by seeing through the robot's eyes and having their movements mirrored. This advancement promises to integrate these robots more deeply into industrial applications, enhancing control and interaction.

title: What’s Changed: 2018 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Data Management Solutions for Analytics
summary: Gartner's 2018 Magic Quadrant for Data Management Solutions for Analytics highlights significant shifts in the market, driven by cloud adoption, Hadoop, and logical data warehouses. The report evaluates 22 providers, noting Oracle's continued leadership, Amazon Web Services' strong ascent, and Snowflake's remarkable improvement into the Challengers quadrant. Several new vendors entered the report, while others were removed, indicating a dynamic and evolving landscape for data management analytics.

title: Qualcomm should negotiate sale to Broadcom, says ISS
summary: Proxy advisory firm Institutional Shareholder Services (ISS) has recommended that Qualcomm negotiate a sale to Broadcom following Broadcom's sweetened $121 billion offer. ISS advised Qualcomm shareholders to vote for four of Broadcom's six director nominees at the upcoming shareholder meeting, suggesting this would encourage a negotiated deal despite Qualcomm's previous resistance. While ISS believes Broadcom's current offer isn't clearly superior to Qualcomm's standalone value in the short term, it views the offer as a reasonable starting point for negotiations.

title: Munsen & Freda Enhance WMG
summary: Warner Music Group has announced a new senior management structure for its technology and data areas. Ralph Munsen has been appointed Chief Information Officer (CIO), while Vinnie Freda will assume the newly created position of Chief Data Officer (CDO). Both will report to CEO Steve Cooper and are tasked with spearheading innovative technological deployment and data-driven decision-making.

title: Birds in a Cage: The Indian Green Card Backlog
summary: This article highlights the immense challenges faced by high-skilled Indian workers in the U.S. due to the green card backlog, often leaving them in immigration limbo for decades. It details the personal struggles of individuals like Vikas and Lokesh Marenayakanapalya with visa renewals, job mobility restrictions, and family uncertainty, advocating for reforms to the per-country cap that exacerbates these delays. Political and corporate voices also weigh in on the need for comprehensive immigration reform to retain talent and support the American tech sector.

title: Roku CEO says memory shortage affected earnings
summary: Roku CEO Anthony Wood stated that memory shortages impacted the company's hardware profitability, despite reporting its most profitable quarter. The company was forced to use more expensive air shipping for NAND memory chips, which are crucial for its hardware and are experiencing rising prices and shortages across the tech industry. This issue may have contributed to a disappointing forecast for Roku.

title: Nokia phones look to the future, and to the past
summary: HMD Global, the maker of Nokia phones, announced an expansion of its product line to include a premium Android smartphone and a modernized version of the classic 8110 "slider" phone. This strategic move aims to build on their significant comeback in the market, having sold approximately 30 million phones and ranking as the world's No. 6 mobile phone seller combined. The company's strategy focuses on reliable, affordable products with the latest innovations, alongside monthly Google security updates.

title: What’s Changed: 2018 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Data Science and Machine-Learning Platforms
summary: Gartner has released its 2018 Magic Quadrant for Data Science and Machine-Learning Platforms, emphasizing machine learning as a key component. The report evaluates 16 providers, highlighting new entrants like Anaconda, Databricks, and TIBCO Software, and significant changes in vendor positioning such as KNIME's improved vision and Alteryx's rise to a leadership position. It also notes regressions for some established players and new challengers in the market.

title: A product Salesforce launched two years ago is now the fastest growing in company history
summary: Salesforce's Field Service Lightning (FSL), launched two years ago, is set to book over $100 million in revenue this year, making it the fastest-growing product in company history. Despite its rapid expansion and market attention, the FSL and broader Service Cloud division have experienced significant leadership turnover. FSL is part of Salesforce's strategy to target specific industries and reach CEO Marc Benioff's goal of $20 billion in revenue by 2022.

title: What’s Changed: 2018 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Analytics and Business Intelligence Platforms
summary: Gartner's 2018 Magic Quadrant for Analytics and Business Intelligence Platforms highlights the mainstream adoption of modern, cloud-based analytics, with a focus on augmented analytics and the shift of responsibility back to IT for self-service functionality. The report evaluates 20 providers, with Tableau, Microsoft, and Qlik identified as leaders, and details changes in vendor inclusion and positions within the quadrants.

title: Digital Transformation: The Information Age Accelerates – Part 2/5
summary: This article, part two of a five-part series, discusses Digital Transformation by placing it in historical context, specifically referencing Daniel Bell's 1973 prediction of the Information Age. It highlights how the convergence of disruptive technologies like Big Data, Elastic Cloud Computing, Artificial Intelligence, and the Internet of Things is accelerating this transformation, using the example of the smart grid to illustrate the impact of IoT. The piece emphasizes the exponential increase in data volume and velocity driven by IoT and how this data, combined with AI, is transforming industries.

title: Gartner Magic Quadrant: Who's Winning In The Data And Machine Learning Space
summary: This article analyzes Gartner's 2018 Magic Quadrant reports for Data Science and Machine-Learning Platforms and Analytics and Business Intelligence Platforms. It highlights key leaders and departures in the BI space, such as Microsoft, Tableau, and Qliktech, and discusses Gartner's cautious stance on AI and Machine Learning adoption, emphasizing the importance of a data strategy. The author also notes discrepancies in vendor rankings between Gartner and other research firms like Forrester.

title: The way we make things is about to fundamentally change
summary: This article discusses how manufacturing is on the cusp of a fundamental change, moving away from global shipping of parts towards localized, digital production. High-speed industrial 3D printers, generative design, reductive decontenting, and assemblies consolidation are highlighted as key drivers of this transformation, leading to more efficient, lighter, and complex products. The author predicts a future of borderless production where digital files travel instead of physical parts, democratizing manufacturing and reducing costs.

title: Apple iPhone X was to start OLED boom, but here’s why it is not working
summary: The iPhone X was expected to drive a boom in OLED screen technology, with suppliers like Samsung ramping up production. However, lower-than-anticipated sales of the iPhone X and high costs of OLED panels compared to LCDs have led to concerns about oversupply and price cuts. Chinese phone makers are also not rushing to adopt OLED, impacting the widespread adoption initially forecasted.

title: Hershey’s sweet spot for Accenture: Consulting company helps implement SAP ERP
summary: The Hershey Company partnered with Accenture to implement SAP S/4/HANA, aiming to streamline manufacturing and supply chain processes and gain real-time customer analytics. This initiative builds on Hershey's existing use of Microsoft Azure and Office 365 for optimizing candy production through intelligent sensors. The move is intended to help Hershey gain better customer insights amidst declining sales and adapt to evolving consumer needs through digital transformation.

title: Gartner reaffirms Microsoft as a leader in Data Management Solutions for Analytics
summary: Gartner has once again positioned Microsoft as a leader in its 2018 Magic Quadrant for Data Management Solutions for Analytics (DMSA), also recognizing the company for Analytics and Business Intelligence Platforms and Operational Database Management Systems. This achievement highlights Microsoft's commitment to innovation in data management, offering solutions like SQL Server 2017 and Azure services to simplify big data processing and analytics. The article emphasizes Microsoft's data platform strengths: productivity, hybrid capabilities, intelligent features, and trusted security.

title: Nokia’s ‘conscious’ factory of the future
summary: Nokia has developed a "conscious factory" concept to transform its manufacturing operations into agile, intelligent, fully-automated, green, and self-learning systems capable of predicting and flexibly preventing supply chain issues. This initiative, driven by digitization, analytics, robotics, and transparency, and supported by a global, data-driven "conscious supply network," is part of a broader supply chain transformation that has significantly improved Nokia's ranking in global supply chain performance. The company is also pioneering a flexible "factory in a box" concept and adopting a customer-centric approach to prepare for the advent of 5G technology and diversify its market.

title: SambaNova Systems Secures $56 Million in Series A Funding
summary: SambaNova Systems emerged from stealth and announced $56 million in Series A funding led by Walden International and GV (formerly Google Ventures), with participation from Redline Capital and Atlantic Bridge Ventures. The company, founded in 2017 based on technology from Stanford University Professors Kunle Olukotun and Chris Ré, is developing next-generation computing platforms to power machine learning and data analytics applications. The investment will be used to expand its team and accelerate the development of its computing platform.

title: Virtual reality project goes underground for pipeline safety
summary: Enbridge, in collaboration with Microsoft and Finger Food Studios, has developed a "digital twin" project utilizing augmented reality to visualize vast amounts of pipeline data. This innovative approach allows engineers to view 3D renderings of pipeline sections, identifying potential hazards like cracks and corrosion more effectively. The goal is to enhance pipeline safety by transforming complex data into an easily digestible visual format, with potential applications for the wider pipeline industry.

title: Virtual reality project goes underground for pipeline safety
summary: Enbridge, in collaboration with Microsoft and Finger Food Studios, has developed a virtual reality "digital twin" to visualize vast amounts of pipeline data in 3D, enhancing pipeline safety and integrity assessments. This innovative application allows engineers to pinpoint potential hazards like dents, cracks, and corrosion more effectively. The initiative represents a significant step towards improving decision-making, training, and maintenance processes within the pipeline industry.

title: The best sector of this bull market is the ‘greatest investment story ever told’
summary: This article highlights that internet stocks have been the best performing sector during the current nine-year bull market, which began after the financial crisis bottom. It notes that while internet investing is often associated with the dot-com era, the current extended bull market has also seen the sector significantly influence nearly every aspect of the economy. The piece was published on the ninth anniversary of the financial crisis bottom.

title: Microsoft Teams IP Desk Phones and Room Phones
summary: This article announces the release of specific Microsoft Teams IP Phones, building on previous support for existing Skype for Business certified phones. It details new personal desk phones from Yealink and AudioCodes, as well as a new category of mobile phone stations. Additionally, the article highlights new room phones from Crestron, Polycom, and Yealink, all integrating the Teams phone application.

title: DowDuPont's Andrew Liveris makes way for Jim Fitterling as new Dow CEO
summary: Andrew Liveris is stepping down from DowDuPont after four decades, with Jim Fitterling set to become the new CEO of Dow when it spins off in 2019. Fitterling, a longtime Dow employee, will be the first openly gay CEO of a major chemical company and has been a proponent of LGBTQ+ rights in corporate America. Howard Ungerleider will serve as president and CFO of the new Dow spinoff.

title: HP Debuts Elite Slice G2 Virtual Meeting Device And 43-inch 4K Display For Businesses
summary: HP has introduced the Elite Slice for Meeting Rooms G2 with Skype Room Systems, a new device designed for virtual meetings and conferences, alongside a 43-inch 4K conferencing display. This system integrates voice, video, and data capabilities into one unit, aiming to simplify collaboration in business environments. HP also touts the device's security features and ease of deployment, with both the SRS and Intel Unite versions shipping in April and June respectively.

title: How Dry Is Texas?
summary: This article details how Microsoft partnered with Nalco Water (an Ecolab company) to implement water efficiency and quality plans at its San Antonio, Texas data center. Facing extreme water stress in the Leon Creek Watershed, Microsoft utilized Nalco Water's 3D TRASAR™ Technology and Water Risk Monetizer tool to optimize water usage, reduce operating costs, and save over $140,000 annually by using recycled water. This initiative highlights Microsoft's commitment to responsible water stewardship and the business case for smart water management in resource-constrained regions.

title: Cognizant, US' Top H-1B Visa Sponsor, Tries to Bury 'Anti-White' Lawsuit
summary: Cognizant Technology Solutions Corp., the leading U.S. sponsor of H-1B visas, is facing a civil rights lawsuit alleging bias against non-Indian workers. Three former employees claim they were replaced by "less qualified" Indians and subjected to discriminatory treatment. Cognizant argues the lawsuit's claims pertain to national origin, not race, and are not covered by federal civil rights law.

title: Salesforce to Acquire MuleSoft, Its Biggest-Ever Buyout Deal
summary: Salesforce is set to acquire MuleSoft for approximately $6.5 billion in its largest-ever buyout deal, which aims to enhance its Platform-as-a-Service portfolio and create a "Salesforce Integration Cloud." This cash-stock transaction reflects a 36% premium for MuleSoft shareholders and is expected to close by July, contributing to Salesforce's goal of reaching $20 billion in revenues by 2022. The acquisition will allow Salesforce to expand its corporate software offerings, compete more effectively with rivals, and leverage MuleSoft's rapid growth and customer base for additional revenue.

title: The Importance of NetApp’s Data Fabric Solution
summary: NetApp's Data Fabric solution, launched in 2014 and based on its ONTAP operating system, helps companies simplify data management across various cloud environments, Edge, and data centers. This solution aids in accelerating digital transformation and modernizing storage by leveraging hybrid cloud power. The move to Data Fabric has expanded NetApp's business opportunities and driven revenue growth, with ONTAP software now available on hyperscale clouds like AWS and Microsoft Azure.

title: After raising $756M in its IPO, Dropbox sees shares jump 36% in market debut
summary: Dropbox Inc. saw its shares jump 36% in its market debut after raising $756 million in its IPO, pricing shares at $21, higher than initial estimates. The company's valuation swelled to over $11 billion, marking the largest tech IPO since Snap Inc. last year. Despite not yet being profitable, the IPO's success is attributed to a Salesforce investment and a relatively small percentage of shares offered, creating scarcity.

title: Ceridian HCM files for IPO in New York, Toronto
summary: Ceridian HCM Holding Inc., a rapidly transforming cloud-software company, has filed to raise up to US$200-million in a dual U.S.-Canadian-listed IPO. The company, largely managed out of Toronto by CEO David Ossip, was originally a unit of IBM and has seen significant growth in its cloud-based business since Ossip's Toronto-based software firm Dayforce Inc. was acquired. This IPO is considered a win for the Canadian tech scene due to Ceridian's strong Canadian ties and leadership.

title: 2018 Gartner Magic Quadrant Application Performance Monitoring Suites: Takeaways
summary: Gartner's 2018 Magic Quadrant for Application Performance Monitoring Suites highlights the growing importance of APM in digital business, expecting 20% of business applications to be monitored by APM suites, up from 5%. The report identifies three key market priorities: digital experience monitoring (DEM), application discovery, tracing, and diagnostics (ADTD), and artificial intelligence for IT operations (AIOps). It evaluates 15 vendors, noting consistent leaders like Dynatrace and CA Technologies, a lack of Visionaries this year, and the significant market growth with revenue of $3.7 billion in 2016.

title: Huawei Dwarfs Ericsson, Nokia on R&D Spend in 2017
summary: Huawei significantly outspent Ericsson and Nokia on research and development in 2017, investing $13.8 billion compared to $4.5 billion and $5.2 billion respectively. This massive R&D budget highlights the challenge for its Western rivals, especially as Huawei ramps up spending on 5G and AI technologies. The article also touches on challenges Huawei faces in the US market due to protectionist measures and national security concerns.

title: UiPath Opens First U.S. Development Center in Bellevue, Wash.
summary: UiPath, a leading enterprise Robotic Process Automation (RPA) software company, announced the opening of its first U.S. product development center in Bellevue, Washington. The company also appointed Param Kahlon, a former Microsoft executive, as chief product officer to lead global product teams and drive automation-enabled business processes, with a focus on integrating AI capabilities into the UiPath platform. This strategic move aims to leverage Bellevue's proximity to Microsoft and its AI talent pool, as UiPath prepares for its next stage of growth and integration of AI into its platform.

title: How Progress Delivers Tools Needed For Organizations To Deploy Cognitive Business Apps
summary: This article details how Progress, a software company established in 1981, provides tools for organizations to develop and deploy cognitive business applications. CEO Yogesh Gupta explains their long-standing mission to support mission-critical application development, evolving from command-line interfaces to modern cloud, mobile, and IoT-based solutions. The company offers products like NativeScript, Kinvey, and DataRPM, which provide flexible frontends, serverless cloud backends, and machine learning capabilities to leverage Big Data for competitive advantage, as demonstrated by their customer success stories with NASA and the Green Bay Packers.

title: Rackspace Positioned in the Leaders Quadrant of 2018 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Public Cloud Infrastructure Managed Service Providers, Worldwide
summary: Rackspace announced its positioning in the Leaders quadrant of Gartner's 2018 Magic Quadrant for Public Cloud Infrastructure Managed Service Providers, Worldwide, for the second consecutive year. This recognition highlights Rackspace's comprehensive portfolio and expertise in delivering next-generation IT services across multiple public and private cloud platforms. The company offers managed cloud services for major providers like AWS, Microsoft Azure, Google Cloud Platform, and Alibaba Cloud, demonstrating its commitment to multi-cloud solutions and customer digital transformation.

title: Microsoft sues Community Health Systems for copyright infringement
summary: Microsoft has filed a lawsuit against Community Health Systems (CHS) for alleged willful copyright infringement. The tech giant claims CHS allowed hospitals it sold to continue using Microsoft software hosted on CHS servers, violating licensing agreements. Microsoft is seeking monetary damages and an injunction to prevent further infringement, stating CHS has been largely unresponsive to verification requests.

title: The AI compilation wars: Intel, Google, Microsoft, Nvidia, IBM and others arm for deep learning acceleration
summary: The article discusses the growing "AI compilation wars" as major tech companies like Intel, Google, Microsoft, Nvidia, and IBM develop cross-platform compilers for deep learning acceleration. These compilers aim to enable AI models built with various front-end tools to run optimally on diverse back-end hardware, fostering a future where AI developers can abstract their models and compile them for hybridized hardware environments. The trend highlights a move towards open-source, framework-agnostic AI development.

title: Building a Big Data pipeline to Process Clickstream Data
summary: This article details Zillow's journey in building an efficient and scalable Big Data pipeline to process clickstream data. It outlines the evolution of their ETL process, from early versions using Amazon Redshift and C# .NET to the current iteration leveraging Apache Spark, Amazon EMR, and Airflow. The focus is on handling massive data volumes, improving processing speed, and achieving reliability through various architectural enhancements.

title: If You File Taxes Using TurboTax, You Could Be Seriously Overpaying
summary: The article highlights that many TurboTax users might be overpaying for tax filing services, as the free federal tax filing option through the IRS Free File program is only available for those with an adjusted gross income of $33,000 or less. This AGI threshold is significantly lower than most other free tax-filing software options, which typically range from $60,000 to $66,000. Millions of taxpayers with AGIs between $30,000 and $75,000 could be affected by this discrepancy and might be able to file for free elsewhere.

title: Sequoia Israel Partner Launches New $50 Million Cybersecurity Fund
summary: Gili Raanan, a partner at Sequoia Capital's Israeli branch, has launched a new $50 million cybersecurity fund called Cyberstarts. The fund will invest in early-stage cybersecurity companies and has raised capital from Sequoia Capital and several prominent cybersecurity entrepreneurs. This initiative aims to leverage the unique Israeli ecosystem where experienced entrepreneurs fund new generations of cybersecurity firms.

title: Free Qualys services give orgs visibility of their digital certs and cloud assets
summary: Qualys announced two new free services, CertView and CloudView, to help organizations gain visibility into their digital certificates and cloud assets. CertView provides continuous inventory and assessment of external-facing digital certificates, helping to mitigate risks from expired or vulnerable SSL/TLS configurations. CloudView offers topological visibility and insight into the security and compliance posture of public cloud infrastructure across major providers like AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud, facilitating asset discovery and continuous security monitoring.

title: Schwab 1000 Index ETF ETF Price, Holdings, & News (NYSEARCA:SCHK)
summary: This article provides detailed information on the Schwab 1000 Index ETF (SCHK), including its price, holdings, key statistics, and recent news. SCHK is an ETF launched in 2017 that tracks the S&P Schwab 1000 index, comprising 1,000 large US-listed stocks. summary: Marillyn A. Hewson, Chairman, President and CEO of Lockheed Martin Corporation, has been named Chief Executive magazine's 2018 Chief Executive of the Year. Her selection will be celebrated at an event at the United Nations in July.

title: Adobe to acquire Magento for $1.68B
summary: Adobe announced its acquisition of Magento for $1.68 billion, aiming to bolster its Experience Cloud with an e-commerce platform that serves both B2B and B2C markets. This move positions Adobe to better compete with Salesforce and could strengthen its existing partnerships with companies like Microsoft. Analysts view the acquisition as a strategic play to complete the customer journey and enhance marketing-to-sale insights, despite Magento's historical focus on SMBs.

title: Quantum Effects At 7/5nm And Beyond
summary: As semiconductor manufacturing nodes shrink to 7/5nm and beyond, quantum effects are becoming increasingly prominent and challenging for the chip industry. These effects, which manifest as unexpected behaviors in electronic devices and signals, necessitate significant adjustments in design rules and manufacturing processes. The article discusses how quantum effects, previously managed by foundries, are now impacting a broader range of companies and require new approaches to mitigate issues like increased variability and changes in device performance.

title: Analog Devices wins prestigious technology award in Dublin
summary: Analog Devices Inc (ADI) received the "Hibernia" award at Ireland’s National Tech Excellence Awards for its significant contributions to the Irish technology sector, including job creation and ecosystem development. title: Microsoft is now more valuable than Alphabet — by about $10 billion
summary: Microsoft has surpassed Alphabet in market capitalization, becoming the world's third most valuable company. This shift occurred as Microsoft's market value reached $749 billion compared to Alphabet's $739 billion, largely driven by significant growth in Microsoft's cloud computing business. Microsoft's stock surged 40 percent over the past 12 months, greatly outpacing Alphabet's gains.

title: Digimarc Barcode has the ‘potential to fundamentally change packaging’
summary: Digimarc Barcode offers a visually imperceptible barcode that can be replicated across packaging, enabling connected devices like smartphones and scanners to identify content. This technology aims to revolutionize retail and packaging by providing enhanced consumer engagement, improved supply chain efficiency, and addressing the limitations of traditional barcodes and packaging real estate. Digimarc's partnerships with GS1 and Microsoft, along with its integration into the SmartLabel app, highlight its potential to become a universal standard for product identification and consumer information access.

title: These tech companies have the most stressed-out workers

title: Golden SAML: How can it abuse SAML authentication protocol?

While not a vulnerability in SAML or AD itself, it demonstrates how domain admin access can be exploited, emphasizing the need for secure and monitored IdP and AD infrastructures for mitigation.

summary: The Tick cyberespionage group has been observed weaponizing secure USB drives to target air-gapped systems, primarily in Japan and South Korea. The malware extracts a hidden malicious file from compromised secure USB drives, aiming to infect critical systems that are not connected to the internet.
